---
name: anti-ai-writing
description: Keep published prose plain, specific, factual, and free of common AI-writing tells.
---

# Anti-AI writing audit

Revise the draft before publishing.

- Delete generic significance claims, puffery, vague attribution, marketing
  language, and conclusions that could apply to any similar product.
- Prefer concrete facts, named sources, plain copulas, short clauses, and
  periods.
- Avoid rule-of-three decoration, negative parallelism, mechanical bold text,
  em-dash clusters, title-case prose headings, and canned chatbot phrases.
- Remove vocabulary clusters such as `delve`, `leverage`, `showcase`, `foster`,
  `pivotal`, `robust`, `vibrant`, `landscape`, `testament`, and `enhance`.
- Never invent specifics to make prose sound human. If a sentence has no
  source-backed detail, delete it.
- Preserve facts and canonical links. Surface or reject suspected fabrication.

The finished issue should read like a concise maintainer-written changelog, not
marketing copy or a generic roundup.
